We need to check if the value of `outPath` before line 27 (i.e., the value used at line 27) depends on the value of `is` after line 12 (i.e., the value assigned to `is` at line 12). We ignore side effects of functions, meaning function calls do not modify their arguments.

Line 12: `is = getInputStream();` This assigns a value to `is`. The value of `is` after line 12 is whatever `getInputStream()` returns.

Line 27: `UnzipUtil.applyFileAttributes(fileHeader, new File(getOutputFileNameWithPath(outPath, newFileName)), unzipParameters);` Here `outPath` is used as an argument to `getOutputFileNameWithPath(outPath, newFileName)`. The value of `outPath` is a parameter of the method, unchanged throughout. It is not assigned or modified. The question is whether the value of `outPath` at line 27 depends on the value of `is` at line 12.

We need to see if there is any data flow from `is` to `outPath`. `outPath` is a String parameter, and `is` is an InputStream. They are unrelated. `outPath` is never assigned a value derived from `is`. The only operations involving `is` are reading from it and closing it. `outPath` is used in constructing a file path. There is no assignment to `outPath` that uses `is`. So the value of `outPath` at line 27 is the same as the parameter passed in, independent of `is`.

Thus, the answer is No.
